agent_note: Two structurally distinct strands. (1) A first-person retrospective memoir strand (Cherry, an actuary) telling her life story in past tense to a directly addressed reader, carrying a live narrating-moment present ('I still think', 'I like to imagine', 'Harvey is dead'). (2) A third-person present-tense strand following other characters (Paula, Eve, Sue, 'the lady') at scene level. The past/present split therefore traces to an identifiable strand split, not to uncertainty. Very heavy gnomic load: this quote page is dominated by second-person universals, aphorisms and essayistic digressions on probability, fate and grief -- 43 of 82 quotes are non-diagnostic gnomic, exactly the adversarial bias METHODOLOGY warns about. Two epigraphs quoting real external authors (Kubler-Ross, Hawking) filed as paratext.
